clue.text: Lad satisfied FA in positional reshuffle — couldn't be better

indicators.note: a reshuffle of positions means these letters are dealt out again in a new order

explanation.surface: A boy content with the Football Association is in a reorganisation of roles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'positional reshuffle' rearranges LAD, SATISFIED and FA, fourteen letters in all; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in perfect health is in a state that could not be improved upon.

clue.text: Feature spot

explanation.surface: A two-word note about spotting a distinguishing mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A small brown mark on the skin is both a facial characteristic and a speck or dot.

clue.text: A Weller getting to New york

explanation.surface: A man named Weller travels to New York.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Weller is Sam Weller's coachman father in Dickens's Pickwick Papers; 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In Dickens's Pickwick Papers the elder Weller, Sam's father, has this first name.

clue.text: Garment to put on in the fall?

definitions.text: Garment to put on in the fall?

parts.words: Garment to put on in the fall?
parts.note: a sleeveless jumper pulled on over the head, read also as the phrase for losing one's footing

explanation.surface: Something warm to wear when autumn arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the fall' suggests autumn, the American season, but the answer split in two is what you do when you fall over. A jumper is a British knitted sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeveless knitted pullover is pulled on over the head, and to stumble on ice is to lose footing.

clue.text: What's the editor's little game, telling his staff to copy?

definitions.text: What's the editor's little game, telling his staff to copy?

parts.words: What's the editor's little game, telling his staff to copy?
parts.note: a children's game where all imitate one person, read as an editor ordering staff to imitate the newspaper's opinion column

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor plays a sly game by ordering staff to imitate.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'leader' is a British newspaper's editorial column, so the children's imitation game becomes an editor's instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's pastime in which everyone imitates whatever the person at the front does.

clue.text: Re-dress in a style to overcome such depression

indicators.note: to style is to fashion or arrange afresh, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Changing your clothes in a new fashion to beat a low mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'style' rearranges RE-DRESS, IN and A; 'to overcome' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloom and dullness amount to a low, cheerless state of mind.

clue.text: Nautical device Lionel, note, got in a twist

indicators.note: getting in a twist means becoming tangled, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Lionel gets tangled up in a ship's rope with a musical note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got in a twist' rearranges LIONEL plus G.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's speed was once measured by a knotted rope paid out astern from a float.

clue.text: Somehow it made Peter think ahead

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are made into the answer in some other way

explanation.surface: Something caused Peter to plan in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' rearranges IT MADE PETER.
explanation.definitionFit: To plan or consider a deed beforehand is to think about it in advance.

clue.text: Unlike 1, one having some trouble

parts.note: a being is one creature or individual

explanation.surface: Someone, unlike the first clue's subject, is having a hard time.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition refers back to 1 across, 'as fit as a fiddle': the opposite is to be unwell. 'having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The opposite of being in perfect health is suffering from sickness.

clue.text: Agree to differ in no calm way

indicators.note: to differ is to be unlike, so the word is changed into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Two people agree to disagree, though heatedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to differ' rearranges AGREE.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen and impatient describes someone acting without calmness.

clue.text: Ancestor of the Black de?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Ancestor of the Black de?' is garbled OCR (the word after 'Black' is cut off); no scan, and a search found no full text.

clue.text: Water colour

explanation.surface: A two-word note on painting in watercolours.
explanation.definitionFit: An inland body of water, and a crimson pigment used by painters.

clue.text: It provides natural complex to the picture

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'It provides natural complex to the picture' is OCR damaged ('complex' apparently cut from a longer word); no scan, so the printed wording cannot be confirmed.
annotationWithheld.clue: It provides natural complex to the picture

clue.text: One you'd expect to be at work on time

definitions.text: One you'd expect to be at work on time

parts.words: One you'd expect to be at work on time
parts.note: a punctual worker, read as one whose craft is working on timepieces

explanation.surface: A dependable employee who is always punctual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on time' seems to mean punctual, but it means working on clocks and watches.
explanation.definitionFit: A maker or repairer of clocks and watches works with timekeeping.

clue.text: Don't exclude a Church leader enthusiastic about it

indicators.note: about means going around, so the word for enthusiastic wraps the church leader

parts.note: the Pope leads the Roman Catholic Church

explanation.surface: A keen churchman should welcome everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests welcoming worshippers, but 'about' is the container signal; 'a' and 'it' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave something available or accessible is not to shut anyone out.

clue.text: Relax with a Spanish bow

explanation.surface: Unwinding with a courteous Spanish bow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To become less stiff or formal is to loosen up.

clue.text: See 5
Unit of force Sir Isaac gravitated

explanation.surface: The physicist behind gravity lends his name to a unit.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Isaac is the scientist who described gravity, hence 'gravitated'.
explanation.definitionFit: The SI unit of force is named after the physicist of gravity, whose surname it shares.

clue.text: Hostile walker I upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or disturbed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone out walking turns aggressive after being disturbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges WALKER and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Belligerent and ready for fighting means openly unfriendly.

clue.text: Examination in which one may see the writing on the wall

definitions.text: Examination in which one may see the writing on the wall

parts.words: Examination in which one may see the writing on the wall
parts.note: the idiom for a warning of doom, read literally as letters on an optician's chart

explanation.surface: A test that reveals a portent of disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the writing on the wall' is an omen of doom, but here it is the chart of letters an optician hangs on the wall.
explanation.definitionFit: An optician's check of vision has the patient read rows of letters on a chart.

clue.text: Handy weapon thrown away

parts.note: a weapon held in the hand and hurled at the enemy, rather than discarded

explanation.surface: A convenient weapon gets discarded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handy' seems to mean convenient but means held in the hand, and 'thrown away' means hurled, not discarded.
explanation.definitionFit: A small explosive device is lobbed by hand at a target.

clue.text: In a flaming temper?

parts.note: a furious mood, read literally as being on fire

explanation.surface: Someone in a towering rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flaming' suggests anger, but read literally it means alight.
explanation.definitionFit: Burning fiercely, or figuratively blazing with passion or anger.

clue.text: Knightly distinction for cuisine of the highest order

explanation.surface: An honour for the very best cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: The blue ribbon of France's old Order of the Holy Spirit gave its name to top-class cooking; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A French knightly order's blue ribbon, later the name for a first-rate cook or dish.

clue.text: See 20
Growth of great actor manager

explanation.surface: The rise of a celebrated theatre manager.
explanation.walkthrough: Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a celebrated Victorian actor-manager who founded RADA; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant growing tall with a trunk, and the surname of Herbert Beerbohm, the Victorian actor-manager.

clue.text: Lewis's counterpart in Italy

parts.note: the Italian form of the first name Louis or Lewis

explanation.surface: An Italian equivalent of a man called Lewis.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian version of the name Louis, also spelt Lewis in English.

clue.text: He's ranked highly in the City

definitions.text: He's ranked highly in the City

parts.words: He's ranked highly in the City
parts.note: a senior civic officer of the City of London corporation

explanation.surface: A high-flyer in the financial district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the City' is the City of London, the financial district, which has its own council of senior elected officers.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior member of a borough or city council, ranking next to the mayor.

clue.text: Become apprehensive in a freshening wind?

explanation.surface: Getting nervous as the wind picks up.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for getting the wind up means to become frightened; read literally it describes a stiffening breeze.
explanation.definitionFit: To get nervous or scared, and literally a light wind strengthening.
